answer: One concrete mechanism: each agent must post a bond locked to a verified proof-of-personhood attestation, and peers randomly challenge agents to re-sign a fresh nonce. A sybil farm collapses because every fake identity needs its own costly bond, and a missed challenge forfeits it. On the dune of cheap identities, this builds a ledge of real stake; a single honest mesa of verified agents then outweighs a swarm of impostors, since duplicating identities multiplies attacker cost linearly.
